about: CHAIN relic_theft (Design/content/chains/relic_theft.md): the sacred thefts of the ninth century, told from the boat. Fourteen cards, the year 828 and after. In 827 Einhard's notary Ratleic took the bones of the martyrs Marcellinus and Peter out of their tomb at Rome by night; a priest of Abbot Hilduin's stole a share on the road for Saint-Medard at Soissons; Einhard had it back at the palace after Easter 828, and on 3 July 828 a part of the relics reached his own house of Saint Bavo at Ganda, where the sick were healed until the end of September (Einhard, Translatio et miracula sanctorum Marcellini et Petri, books I, II and IV; Design/content/dossiers/ganda.md). Einhard reckoned fifteen days by boat between Ganda and his house on the Main. This chain puts that box in the player's boat. A deacon of Mulinheim (Otbert, invented) hires a Frisian on the Rhine; a priest of Saint-Medard (Gozhelm, invented) offers two thousand pennies for the box to lose its way to the Seine; a seller of bones (Lupicinus, invented) has two bundles that weigh the same; a blind man of the coast (Germar, real: Translatio IV) asks for passage; and on an ebb at the Scheldt mouth the deacon goes up to the church for an hour. Three endings: Saint Bavo (what really happened: ch_relic_theft_end_ganda), Soissons (history changed: ch_relic_theft_end_soissons, changed_marcellinus_ganda), and two saints (both houses have a box: ch_relic_theft_end_two_saints), and a last card in 830 or later, when Einhard's book is being copied. Cards with weight 0 come only when another card names them in 'then'. Words: Data/writing/chain_relic_theft.json (an outcome text for every option, keys '...out_<option>', is named in each option's note). Nothing is quoted from any translation. (?) marks what was not checked against a source. A draft for the user to overwrite. Written 6 Oct 2026.

cards.note: Step 1, the start: drawn at Mogontia, Colonia, Noviomagus, Dorestad or Traiectum from April to December 828. Otbert (Ot- + -bert, invented), a deacon of Mulinheim, Einhard's house on the Main, has a box for Saint Bavo's at Ganda. Sources: Einhard, Translatio IV (relics sent to Saint Bavo's; they came 3 July 828: dossiers/ganda.md); Einhard's letter of 830 reckoning fifteen days by boat from Ganda to the Main (dossiers/ganda.md [5]); pilgrims riding in merchant boats on the Main (dossiers/mogontia.md, from the Translatio). Who carried the Ganda relics, and in what boat, no source says: the hiring of a Frisian is ours (?). Einhard was abbot of Saint Bavo's from 819 and ruled it from the palace. The riddle is Symphosius 4, the key (riddles_793.json). Every option takes the box aboard. Sets ch_relic_theft_1, ch_relic_theft_carrying; ch_relic_theft_knows or ch_relic_theft_alms by the choice.

cards.note: Step 2: drawn at Colonia, Noviomagus, Dorestad or Traiectum with the box aboard. Gozhelm (Goz- + -helm, invented), a priest of Saint-Medard at Soissons, Abbot Hilduin's house. Sources: the relics of Saint Sebastian came from Rome to Saint-Medard in 826 by the pope's gift (Annales regni Francorum 826); Hilduin, archchaplain, abbot of Saint-Denis and of Saint-Medard, sent his priest Hunus with Einhard's notary, and Hunus took a share of Marcellinus on the road and carried it to Soissons; Einhard had it back from Hilduin at the palace of Aachen after Easter 828 (Translatio I-II; the week from memory (?)). That thieves of relics said the saint consented, or no man could have lifted him, is the common plea of the translation stories (P. Geary, Furta Sacra, 1978, as a guide only). The fair of Saint-Denis from 9 October and its wine: chain wine_fleet. Gozhelm's offer is ours. Sets ch_relic_theft_2; ch_relic_theft_loyal or ch_relic_theft_earnest by the choice.

cards.note: Step 4: scheduled three days after step 2, and drawn at any landing while the box is aboard and before the ebb of step 6. It may be passed over; then the road of two boxes stays shut. Lupicinus (a late Roman name, invented) sells bones with names. Sources: the great capitulary of 789 (Admonitio generalis) c. 42, no false names of martyrs, and c. 79, against wanderers who deceive the people (story/unlocks_793.json unlock_relic_false_bone); from 827 Roman bones came north in number, and the deacon Deusdona went on supplying the abbeys of the Rhine and Main (Translatio; Rudolf of Fulda for the later journeys (?); unlocks_793.json unlock_relic_roman_martyr, 60 d). The wax at Ganda: Einhard's letter asking for wax because the honey was short (dossiers/ganda.md [5]). The two blank bundles are ours. Sets ch_relic_theft_4; ch_relic_theft_false_bone and the shared unlock_relic_false_bone, or the shared unlock_relic_roman_martyr.

cards.note: Step 5: drawn at Walichrum or Andoverpis with the box aboard. Germar is REAL: among those healed at Saint Bavo's in the summer of 828 Einhard's fourth book names Germar, a blind man 'from the sea-coast of the Frisians near the mouth of the river Scheldt' (Translatio IV, the Ganda report; dossiers/ganda.md [6]). How he came to Ganda, the child who leads him and his penny are ours. Einhard had the cures written down house by house with names, places and days, and put the sheets into his book. Every option names step 6 for the next day at the same landing. Sets ch_relic_theft_5; ch_relic_theft_germar if he is taken aboard.

cards.note: Step 6, the turn: Walichrum or Andoverpis, the day after step 5 (scheduled there, and drawn). If the player sails for Ganda before it comes, the box simply arrives (step 10) and the ending is Saint Bavo's. Four roads: wait (to Ganda); cast off with the box (the theft; the lasting cost ch_relic_theft_sacrilege); two boxes (only with the bone seller's bundles: step 7 by 'then'); or go up to the church and tell the deacon (the honest hard road, only for a man who took no earnest: the lasting cost is the enmity of the archchaplain's house while he holds his office, ch_relic_theft_hilduin_enmity for 700 days: Hilduin lost his offices in the autumn of 830). Sources: the church in the fort at Andoverpis is Amand's, of the seventh century; a church at Walichrum is assumed (?). Hilduin's seal and his power at the palace: he was archchaplain from about 819 to 830. That a count's man would not hold a priest with that seal is ours. Sets ch_relic_theft_6 and one of ch_relic_theft_to_ganda, ch_relic_theft_stole, ch_relic_theft_denounced.

cards.note: Step 7 (only by 'then' from step 6, the same night). The bone seller's two bundles and the martyrs' two lie side by side. False to Soissons: the martyrs go on to Ganda as they really did, and Saint-Medard shows nobody's bones (ch_relic_theft_real_at_ganda). True to Soissons: Ganda gets nobody's bones under the true labels (ch_relic_theft_real_at_soissons, changed_marcellinus_ganda, ch_relic_theft_sacrilege). Or neither. Sources: relics were kept in silk with a written label (the authentic) tied to each; the ninth-century labels of Sens and Chelles survive (from memory (?)). That Saint-Medard afterwards claimed to hold relics of Marcellinus and Peter is said of the house's later writings (?). The 900 d is what a horse can carry unnoticed; ours. Sets ch_relic_theft_7 and ch_relic_theft_swapped or ch_relic_theft_to_ganda; clears the shared unlock_relic_false_bone when the bundles leave the boat.

cards.note: Step 8: drawn under way after the ebb of step 6, on any road, while the box is aboard. It may be passed over. The danger is weather only, and it warns: the men speak first, and the sure choice costs a day. For the thief it is the last easy place to turn back (ch_relic_theft_repented: the box goes to Ganda after all, as Hilduin's share went back to Einhard). Sources: the bloody liquid at Michelstadt (Translatio I); a candle of a sick man's own weight or height vowed to a saint is common in the miracle books (chain storm_vow has the custom in full). No Northmen: the first recorded raid on Walcheren is 837. Sets ch_relic_theft_8.

cards.note: Step 9, the thief's road only: drawn at Quentovic or Rotomagus with the stolen box aboard. It may be passed over by a boat that does not call. The deacon has written to the bishops of the coast. A man who is not believed pays and is marked (ch_relic_theft_marked); the box is not taken from him, for no clerk seizes what goes to the archchaplain's house. He may also give it up here and carry it back (ch_relic_theft_repented). Sources: Quentovic's toll and the king's officer over the Channel ports (ports_793.json; harbour.tollman.frankish); Rotomagus is the archbishop's city. The deacon's letter is ours, in the manner of Einhard's own letters to bishops (dossiers/mogontia.md, letter VIII to Otgar). Sets ch_relic_theft_9.

cards.note: Step 10: Ganda, when the box comes there (every road but the thief's). What really happened: on 3 July 828 the relics of Marcellinus and Peter reached Saint Bavo's, and the sick were healed there until 30 September; among them the blind girl Hartlinda of Furnes, Eberald and Gundrada, serfs of the house, Liodold of Alphen on two crutches, and Germar, blind, from the Frisian coast by the Scheldt mouth (Translatio IV; dossiers/ganda.md [6]). Erembert, the abbot's steward (vicedominus) at Ganda, is real, from Einhard's letters; that he held the office in 828 is assumed (?). If nobody's bones lie in the box (ch_relic_theft_real_at_soissons) Germar is not healed. The balance of the freight is paid; the rest waits sixty days for the abbot's answer (the timed flag ch_relic_theft_wait). Sets ch_relic_theft_10; clears ch_relic_theft_carrying.

cards.note: ENDING 'ganda', what really happened: Ganda, sixty days or more after the box came (drawn once the timed flag ch_relic_theft_wait has run out), on the honest roads and the road of the thief who turned back. The martyrs lie at Saint Bavo's and the cures are written down. Sources: Translatio IV (the Ganda report; cures to 30 September; Saint Bavo's feast is 1 October); Einhard ordering the dues of his Ganda abbeys taken 'in full and in good silver', and asking for wax because the honey had been short (letters, dossiers/ganda.md [5]); the lay village on the Scheldt bank by the abbey from the early ninth century, with its bank plots (dossiers/ganda.md [7]); cloths laid on a saint's tomb and given away as relics (brandea) are the old Roman custom (Gregory the Great's letter to Constantina (?)); the emperor's writing for merchants who serve the palace is the praeceptum negotiatorum of 828 (Formulae imperiales no. 37: toll-free except at Quentovic, Dorestad and the passes; from memory (?)). Grand rewards: unlock_plot_ganda, or unlock_relic_marcellinus_cloth; on the hard road unlock_title_kings_protection and the plot. Sets ch_relic_theft_end_ganda.

cards.note: ENDING 'soissons', history changed by the player: Parisius, when the stolen box comes to the landing of Saint-Denis (the voyage round by the Channel and up the Seine is the wait). Hilduin was abbot of Saint-Denis as well as of Saint-Medard, and the abbey held the tolls of its October fair (Pippin's judgement of 753; chain wine_fleet, which also sets unlock_title_saint_denis_man and unlock_plot_parisius). In truth Hilduin's house had a stolen share of Marcellinus for some months and gave it back; here it gets the Ganda box and keeps it. Thefts of relics were written up as the saint's own wish: the story Gozhelm is writing is the kind Einhard himself wrote of the night at Rome. Lasting costs: ch_relic_theft_sacrilege, ch_relic_theft_einhard_enmity (the abbot of Ganda knows a Frisian boat did it), changed_marcellinus_ganda. The third choice takes little and leaves the weight behind. Sets ch_relic_theft_end_soissons; clears ch_relic_theft_carrying.

cards.note: ENDING 'two_saints': Ganda, sixty days or more after the box came, on the road of two boxes. Two houses show the martyrs Marcellinus and Peter, and only the shipman knows which has them. With ch_relic_theft_real_at_ganda the cures are at Ganda as they really were and Saint-Medard has nobody's bones; with ch_relic_theft_real_at_soissons it is the other way and history is changed (changed_marcellinus_ganda, set in step 7). Sources: two houses claiming one saint is common in the age (the head of John the Baptist; Saint Denis at Paris and at Regensburg in the eleventh century; from memory (?)); each house wrote its own miracles. The finger bone held back is ours: Hunus held back more. Confessing costs the Soissons silver and wins the abbey's protection (immunity of Saint Bavo's: Louis the Pious, 13 April 819, dossiers/ganda.md [9]). Grand rewards: unlock_relic_peter_finger, or unlock_title_st_bavos_man. The lasting cost of silence is ch_relic_theft_secret. Sets ch_relic_theft_end_two_saints.

cards.note: Step 14, the afterword: drawn from 830 at Ganda, Mogontia, Colonia, Traiectum, Dorestad or Parisius after any ending. Einhard wrote the Translation and Miracles of Marcellinus and Peter in four books about 830 to 831 (the date from memory (?)): the night at the tomb, Hunus's theft, the bloody liquid, the dreams, and the cures house by house. He names no boat and no shipman for Ganda (true). Hilduin took the side of the emperor's sons in 830, lost his offices that autumn and was sent away; he had Saint-Denis again within a year or two (Astronomer, Vita Hludowici c. 45 (?)). Einhard was at Saint Bavo's, sick, in the spring of 830 (dossiers/ganda.md). The riddle is Aldhelm's book chest (riddles_793.json). A lamp before the martyrs clears what the theft left hanging (ch_relic_theft_sacrilege, ch_relic_theft_secret, ch_relic_theft_einhard_enmity). Sets ch_relic_theft_14; unlock_heirloom_einhards_leaf if the leaf is copied.

cards.title: The book
cards.intention: A monk is copying a new book in the porch for the light: the abbot Einhard's own account of how the martyrs came out of Rome and what they did afterwards. He reads a little of it aloud to anyone who stands still.
